root_cause: The compact ContextRulesChip Popover contains tooltip-bearing controls. With Open full view or Reset all focused, Radix TooltipContent installs the top DismissableLayer and consumes the first Escape, leaving the popover open. A real component test observed the tooltip close while the dialog remained. The focused key event reaches PopoverContent with defaultPrevented=true before document-level dismissal.
hypotheses_falsified: No other dialog is needed: the exact real Popover+Tooltip chain reproduces in isolation.
Popover dismissal itself works when no tooltip is above it; the failing first Escape is taken by TooltipContent.
repair: ContextRulesChip routes Escape from a DOM-contained focused control to its own open state at the PopoverContent boundary, while portaled nested surfaces retain their own key path.

verification.evidence: pnpm exec vitest run context/react/context-react.test.tsx -t 'Escape dismisses the compact popover' showed assertion failure on old source: dialog remained after tooltip closed. On new source, pnpm exec vitest run context/react/context-react.test.tsx --reporter=dot passed 38/38. plant.py mutation replacing Escape check with true produced named RED in ArrowDown case and restored bytes identically. Combined inline-editor Escape test proves draft canceled without rule write and unchanged original after reopen; mutating InlineMaxInput skip.current=true to false produced named RED and restored bytes identically.

inline_editor_boundary: Initial proposed assertion that the outer compact popover remains open after editor Escape failed on existing Radix behavior; the product handler did not receive that key. Existing behavior may close the parent, so the final guard asserts the supported contract: Escape cancels the draft, never writes a rule, and reopening shows the original value.
